g12-history-uh9-t1.overview: Indigenous Knowledge: Definition and Unique Characteristic Features sits inside Indigenous Knowledge Systems and Heritages of Ethiopia. Indigenous knowledge and the heritages of Ethiopia close Grade 12 History Unit 9 in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it defines indigenous knowledge and lists its unique features, from local and holistic to intergenerational. Then it shows Ethiopia’s rich systems in farming, medicine, architecture, and governance. Next, it explains heritage, its values, and the difference between tangible and intangible culture. Also, it covers festivals, UNESCO sites, and national parks across the country. Students will also learn how this knowledge supports sustainable development today.
objectives: Define indigenous knowledge and list its unique features.
Explain its value for sustainable development.
Describe Ethiopia’s traditional systems in farming, medicine, and governance.
Distinguish tangible from intangible cultural heritage.
Discuss the main festivals and heritage sites of Ethiopia.

  • First, indigenous knowledge as local wisdom built up over generations outside formal schooling.
  • Also its unique features: local, holistic, cumulative, spiritual, and shared by word of mouth.
  • Ethiopia’s own systems, from the Gada democracy to Konso terracing and Afar Dagu.
